verdicts.rationale: The Goldfeld-Quandt test and the White test are alternative diagnostic methods used to test for heteroskedasticity under different assumptions.
Understanding heteroskedasticity is essential for seeing why standard errors become unreliable and biased in regression analysis.
The Goldfeld-Quandt test is specifically applied to detect the presence of heteroskedasticity in regression error terms.
Detecting heteroskedasticity using the Breusch-Pagan test explains why standard errors might be unreliable in your regression output.
Standard errors remain reliable under homoskedasticity, whereas heteroskedasticity causes them to become underrepresented and unreliable.
The White test helps identify the heteroskedasticity that causes standard errors to be incorrectly estimated.
The Goldfeld-Quandt test checks the null hypothesis of homoskedasticity against the alternative of changing error variance.
